name: Kentucky
rateNote: No fixed statewide rate — purchaser sets rate per certificate within statutory bounds
bidMethod: Highest bidder — sheriff sells Certificates of Delinquency
keyNotes: Sheriff sells Certificates of Delinquency — investors purchase tax bills directly
50-day notice requirement after purchase to notify owner
Circuit court foreclosure required to obtain deed — no automatic conversion
Owner can redeem at any time before foreclosure sale is complete
High redemption rate — most certificates pay out as interest income
summary: Kentucky conducts in-person sealed bid sales at the county level. No online bidding. 1-year redemption before foreclosure can proceed. Statute: KRS §134.420.
typeWhy: Kentucky sells tax lien certificates through in-person sealed bid sales at the county level. The investor purchases the lien while the owner retains title during the 1-year redemption window. KRS §134.420.
rateWhy: Kentucky imposes a 12% annual interest rate on tax lien certificates plus additional statutory penalties on redemption. KRS §134.420.
notBeginnerReason: In-person only, no online bidding, sealed bid format makes it hard to gauge competition.
beginnerTip: Jefferson (Louisville) and Fayette (Lexington) counties have the best inventory. The sealed bid format works in your favor in rural counties — less competition means your opening bid often wins.
risks: Sealed bid format makes it impossible to know competitor bids
ddExtra: Visit the property in person before submitting a bid — no online verification is sufficient
Verify lien priority in the county records office
Confirm the redemption period has not been extended for any reason

auctionSignup.platform: County Sheriff or County Clerk (in-person, sealed bid)
steps: Find your target county's sheriff or clerk at kycourts.net
Contact the office to confirm the upcoming sale date and request the property list
Obtain and complete the sealed bid form — submit in person by the deadline
Attend the opening — winners are announced publicly
auctionSignup.depositInfo: Typically cashier's check at time of bid submission.

tylerCompliance.summary: Status pending — monitoring for legislative action.
tylerCompliance.details: This state compliance with Tyler v. Hennepin County (2023) is currently being monitored. Aurigen tracks legislative updates, pending bills, and court decisions that affect tax sale surplus requirements. Check back for updates.

auction.frequency: Annual — mid-July (90–135 days after bills filed with county clerk on April 15)
auction.platform: County Clerk's office — each county independently. No statewide platform.
auction.bidMethod: Premium bid — certificates sold to first purchaser offering to pay full amount
auction.note: KY uses premium bid per KRS 134.450 — if total offers exceed 10% of total dollar amount or $200K, special lot allocation process applies
auction.depositSelection: Random drawing determines selection order at start of sale

registration.stateLevel: Register with KY Dept of Revenue (Form 62A370A). $250 fee. Required if: >3 certs in a county, >5 statewide, or >$10,000 invested. Application deadline: May 15, 2026 for 2026 sales.
registration.countyLevel: Separate registration required at each county clerk's office. Deadlines set by county.
registration.saleDatesUrl: https://revenue.ky.gov/Property/pages/third-party-purchaser.aspx (County Clerk Delinquent Tax Sale Dates — updated 3/16/26)

otc.name: Prior-Year Certificate Purchase (OTC)
otc.description: Certificates from prior years not yet foreclosed — available year-round from county clerk
otc.process: Contact county clerk directly. Prior-year certs available anytime from clerk.
otc.note: Kenton County confirmed: prior-year certs available year-round at kentondeeds.com

subTax.name: Subsequent Tax Payment
subTax.process: Certificate holder may pay subsequent delinquent taxes — added to certificate balance

redemption.period: 1 year from date taxes became delinquent (i.e., Jan 1 of year following assessment)
redemption.noForeclosureBefore: Cannot commence foreclosure action until 1 year after delinquency date (KRS §134.546)
redemption.note50DayNotice: Within 50 days of cert delivery, purchaser must mail notice to property owner (KRS §134.490). Annual notice required thereafter.

deedPath.name: Master Commissioner's Deed (via Circuit Court foreclosure)
deedPath.process: Certificate holder files foreclosure lawsuit in Circuit Court after 1-year redemption. Master Commissioner conducts foreclosure sale. Court confirms.
deedPath.belowAppraisedValue: If property sells for less than 2/3 of appraised value at foreclosure — owner gets additional 6-month redemption at 10% interest (KRS §426.530)
deedPath.note: Louisville (Jefferson County): city uses KRS Chapter 91 mass foreclosure process — separate procedure via City petitioner

surplus.name: Surplus Proceeds
surplus.process: Distributed by court in priority order after foreclosure sale — former owner receives any remaining surplus
surplus.note: Tyler v. Hennepin applies — KY court process distributes surplus to former owners

es.summary: Kentucky realiza ventas selladas en persona a nivel de condado. Sin pujas en línea. Redención de 1 año antes de que pueda proceder la ejecución. Estatuto: KRS §134.420.
es.typeWhy: Kentucky es un estado de gravamen porque los condados venden certificados de gravamen fiscal en formato de puja sellada con un período de redención de 1 año (KRS §134.420).
es.rateWhy: La tasa del 12% más penalidades adicionales proporciona un retorno moderado. El formato de puja sellada significa que la tasa efectiva no se reduce por competencia visible (KRS §134.420).
es.notBeginnerReason: Solo en persona, sin pujas en línea, el formato de puja sellada dificulta evaluar la competencia.
es.beginnerTip: Jefferson (Louisville) y Fayette (Lexington) tienen el mejor inventario. El formato sellado funciona a su favor en condados rurales — menos competencia.
risks: Solo en persona — no puede participar remotamente
El formato sellado hace imposible conocer pujas de competidores
ddExtra: Visite la propiedad en persona antes de enviar una puja
Verifique la prioridad del gravamen en la oficina de registros del condado
Confirme que el período de redención no haya sido extendido

auctionSignup.platform: Sheriff del condado o Secretario del condado (en persona, puja sellada)
steps: Encuentre el sheriff o secretario de su condado en kycourts.net
Contacte la oficina para confirmar la próxima fecha y solicitar la lista de propiedades
Obtenga y complete el formulario de puja sellada — envíe en persona antes del plazo
Asista a la apertura — los ganadores se anuncian públicamente
auctionSignup.depositInfo: Normalmente cheque de caja al momento de envío.
